title: Hosted API enterprise triage runbook for multi-output admission control
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Purpose: provide a reproducible, SLA-aware triage runbook for enterprise feature intake that involve multi-output Hosted API requests (chat + streaming + tool/function calls + structured outputs). The goal is to enable rapid, consistent decisions (accept / needs design / deny or escalate to Dedicated/Private) using weighted signals from compliance, latency/throughput needs, data residency, and quality certification prerequisites.

Scope: enterprise non-bug feature requests only; excludes pure SDK changes and infra-only capacity requests. Covers: onboarding checklist, automated priority scoring, manual review playbook, required artifacts, fallback recommendations (model variants, reduce streaming fidelity, structured-output schema relaxation), and handoff to ENG/Design/Security.

Deliverables:
- A 7-step triage checklist for intake reviewers (PMs + Solutions Eng)
- Priority scoring template (CSV/Sheet) with weights and thresholds documented
- Decision matrix mapping customer signals to outcome lanes (Self-serve Hosted / Hosted with SLA / Dedicated reserved / Private deployment required)
- Example completed intake for three archetypal customers (SaaS PLG, regulated enterprise, platform team)
- Integration plan to wire signals into the intake form (Drive -> intake service) and a Slack notification for escalations

Key signals and rationale:
- SLA sensitivity (low/medium/high) -> high weight (customer paying for SLA or compliance requirement)
- Data classification (public/internal/confidential/regulated) -> forces Private or Dedicated when regulated
- Streaming fidelity requirement (realtime vs batchy streaming) -> affects runtime selection and backlog scheduling
- Toolcall surface area (# external tools, external API integrations) -> increases operational risk, triggers security review
- Structured-output certification need (schema validation, deterministic outputs) -> requires eval suite and regression gates
- Expected QPS and latency SLO -> routing: dedicated pools vs shared hosted tier
- Commercial commitment & roadmap fit -> tie-breaker, affects priority uplift

Trade-offs considered:
- Tight thresholds reduce risk but push more customers to Dedicated/Private increasing sales friction. We recommend a two-week probation window for hosted SLOs before migration.
- Requiring full structured-output evals upfront increases time-to-onboard; accept staged certification (sampling + automated regressions) for mid-tier customers.

Acceptance criteria for "Hosted with SLA":
- Completed intake form with signals populated
- Security checklist signed-off (SRE/Security)
- Eval run shows <5% regression on canonical prompt set
- Agreed fallback routes (model variant, degraded streaming quality) documented

Metrics to monitor post-acceptance:
- Onboard-to-production time (target: <= 10 business days)
- Number of escalations to Dedicated/Private (target: <= 20% of enterprise intakes)
- First-week error/latency regressions (target: 95th percentile latency within committed SLO)
